Mutating joins for tbl_gpu (left_join(), inner_join(), full_join(), right_join())

Source: R/join.R
mutating-joins.Rd

Equi and non-equi joins on the GPU, with dplyr's by=/keep=/ na_matches=/multiple=/unmatched=/relationship= semantics. Row order, key coalescing, suffixing and every cardinality check follow dplyr::left_join() and friends. See "Details" for what runs on the GPU and what runs in dplyr on the CPU.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
left_join(
  x,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  copy = FALSE,
  suffix = c(".x", ".y"),
  ...,
  keep = NULL,
  na_matches = "na",
  multiple = "all",
  unmatched = "drop",
  relationship = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
inner_join(
  x,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  copy = FALSE,
  suffix = c(".x", ".y"),
  ...,
  keep = NULL,
  na_matches = "na",
  multiple = "all",
  unmatched = "drop",
  relationship = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
full_join(
  x,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  copy = FALSE,
  suffix = c(".x", ".y"),
  ...,
  keep = NULL,
  na_matches = "na",
  multiple = "all",
  relationship = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
right_join(
  x,
  y,
  by = NULL,
  copy = FALSE,
  suffix = c(".x", ".y"),
  ...,
  keep = NULL,
  na_matches = "na",
  multiple = "all",
  unmatched = "drop",
  relationship = NULL
)

Arguments

x, y

tbl_gpu objects to join. If y is not a tbl_gpu, set copy = TRUE to upload it automatically (tbl_gpu(y)).

by

Join specification: NULL (natural join on every common column name), an unnamed character vector (c("a", "b"), matched by identical name on both sides), a named character vector (c("lx" = "ry"), for differently-named keys), or a dplyr::join_by() spec. Key columns whose types differ are cast to their common type for matching, as in dplyr (integer/double/logical, factor/character, Date/POSIXct), and a pair with no common type raises dplyr_error_join_incompatible_type when the verb is called. by = character() (deprecated in dplyr 1.1.0, warns once) is a cross join with the usual multiple=/relationship=/ unmatched= rules. join_by() conditions run on the GPU: equality (a, a == b), inequality (>=, >, <=, <, and the between()/within()/overlaps() helpers built from them), one closest() rolling condition next to any number of == conditions, and inequalities between two string columns. Two closest() conditions, closest() next to another inequality, and factor/logical/Date-vs-POSIXct rolling keys run in dplyr on the CPU (see options(cuplyr.fallback = ) to be told), with the same result as dplyr.

copy

Whether to upload a non-tbl_gpu y via tbl_gpu().

suffix

Length-2 character vector used to disambiguate colliding non-key column names (default c(".x", ".y")). As in dplyr, an already-taken suffixed name gets suffixed again (val.y.y) rather than silently colliding. A suffix with an empty element (c("", "")) that still leaves two columns with the same name runs in dplyr on the CPU, which gives dplyr's result (the right column replaces the left one, and the output has one column fewer).

...

Not used; dplyr itself requires these to be empty.

keep

Whether to keep both sides' join key columns in the output. NULL (the default) resolves per condition, as in dplyr: an equi condition's key columns coalesce to one (the right-side copy is dropped), while a non-equi condition's columns are always kept on both sides (there is no single coalesced value for an inequality). Explicit keep = FALSE is only allowed when every condition is equi (otherwise it is dplyr's error); explicit keep = TRUE keeps and suffixes every key column on both sides.

na_matches

"na" (default): an NA key matches another NA key, like base::merge(). "never": NA keys never match anything, including another NA.

multiple

How to resolve a left/right row matching more than one row on the other side: "all" (default, every match kept), "any", "first", or "last", all on the GPU (the undocumented "error" and "warning" run in dplyr on the CPU). The default "all" costs nothing extra. Under right/full joins a y row that no kept pair uses is listed once as unmatched.

unmatched

How to handle rows with no match: "drop" (default) or "error" (raises dplyr's dplyr_error_join_matches_nothing/ dplyr_error_join_matches_remaining conditions, including the offending row number). full_join() has no unmatched= parameter, as in dplyr (it never drops a row).

relationship

Optional cardinality assertion: NULL (default – emits dplyr's own many-to-many advisory warning whenever both sides have a genuine duplicate, for equality joins called directly; never for inequality/overlap joins or indirect calls, as in dplyr), "one-to-one", "one-to-many", "many-to-one", or "many-to-many" (silences the advisory warning). A violation raises dplyr's dplyr_error_join_relationship_* condition, with its class vector and first-offending-row bullet.

Value

A tbl_gpu with dplyr's own row/column contract for the given join type. right_join()'s row order is x-matched rows (in x's own order) followed by any unmatched y rows appended last.

Details

On the GPU

  • Equi joins (join_by(a), by = "col", by = c(a = "b")): a hash join, with the rows put in dplyr's order.

  • Non-equi and mixed join_by() conditions (>=, >, <=, <, and their between()/within()/overlaps() forms).

  • na_matches=, multiple=, unmatched= and relationship=, with dplyr's condition classes and message text.

  • join_by(closest(...)) rolling joins: exactly one closest() condition (>=, >, <=, <) plus == conditions, on integer, double, Date, POSIXct or string rolling keys. Each row of x finds its closest rows of y without building the whole inequality join. Every y row tied at the closest value is returned, and multiple=/unmatched=/relationship= act on those matches, as in dplyr.

  • A non-equi condition comparing two string columns: strings compare in byte (C locale) order.

In dplyr on the CPU

These, among others, run in dplyr and the result comes back to the GPU (with a notice under options(cuplyr.fallback = "warn")):

  • Two closest() conditions, closest() next to another inequality, and rolling keys that are factors, logicals or a Date against a POSIXct.

  • A non-equi condition comparing a string with a non-string column.

  • Factor keys whose levels differ between x and y.

  • A Date key joined to a POSIXct key in a zone other than UTC (dplyr compares the date as local midnight of that zone).

  • suffix = c("", ...) when it would still produce a genuine duplicate output column name.

  • nest_join() (not one of the four verbs documented here) always runs on the CPU: its result holds a list column, which a GPU table can't hold.
